Represents a day of the week (Sunday..Saturday). Constructible from integers or time_points; supports arithmetic with date::days; c_encoding() gives 0..6 with Sunday=0; iso_encoding() gives 1..7 with Monday=1.

Represents the last day of a given month (e.g., March/last). Used to compute actual last day considering leap years when combined with a year.
Represents a specific weekday occurrence within a month (e.g., May/Tuesday[2]). ok() validates both parts.
Represents the last occurrence of a weekday in a given month (e.g., May/Friday[last]).

RAII helper that saves and restores a basic_ios stream’s formatting state on destruction. Internal utility.

Compile-time greatest common divisor metafunction used in duration rounding helper machinery. Internal utility.

Metafunction that detects if converting between two duration periods can be done without overflow in intermediate computations; provides an adjusted ratio type when overflow would occur. Internal utility.
Internal tag type used to disambiguate accessors/mutators for hh_mm_ss seconds in specific contexts. Not intended for public consumption.
Compile-time computation of number of decimal digits required to represent the fractional part of 1/denominator, truncated to a limit. Used to format subseconds.
Compile-time power-of-10 helper for formatting fractional seconds.

Formats a duration down to fractional seconds with a compile-time-determined precision; splits into whole seconds and subseconds for streaming. Internal utility, but part of the header’s interface for formatting.
Breaks a duration into sign, hours, minutes, and seconds (with fractional precision). Provides formatting and reconstruction back to a precise duration. time_of_day is an alias to hh_mm_ss.
Small fixed-size compile-time string with concatenation operators used to build unit suffixes and formatting strings in a constexpr-friendly way. Internal utility.
Traits struct to convert arithmetic values to std::basic_string of CharT for streaming durations with unit suffixes. Internal utility.
Aggregates parsed/formatting fields: a calendar date (ymd), weekday, and a time-of-day (tod). Used by to_stream/from_stream formatting/parsing APIs.
Tag type representing the last ISO week of a given ISO year. Used with operator/ composition (e.g., y/last to form year_lastweek). No data members.
ISO weekday (1=Mon ... 7=Sun) wrapper. Convertible to/from date::weekday and from sys_days/local_days. Provides arithmetic with days and validation.
ISO year wrapper around a 16-bit signed value with range/validation, leap-year detection (based on ISO week rules), arithmetic with years, and min/max helpers.
ISO week number (1..53). Supports increment/decrement and arithmetic with weeks. Validation via ok().
Pair of ISO year and week number. Validates that week number is within the year's ISO-week count. Supports shifting by years.
Represents the last ISO week of a specific year (W52 or W53, depending on leap-week). Provides access to year and computed weeknum.
Combination of ISO week number and weekday (e.g., W03-Wed). Validates both components.
Represents a weekday within the last ISO week of a year (e.g., W last-Fri).
Specific date identified by ISO year, the last ISO week of that year, and a weekday. Convertible to sys_days/local_days, supports year shifting.

Full ISO week-date (year-week-weekday). Constructible from components, from a year_lastweek_weekday, or from sys_days/local_days. Convertible back to sys_days/local_days; includes validation and year shifting.
Tag type used to denote the last day or last weekday of a month in composition operators (e.g., m/last, y/m/last). It carries no data and only serves as a compile-time selector.

Represents a month-of-year (1..12) for the Julian calendar. Supports arithmetic with months duration, comparisons, streaming, and validation via ok().
Represents a Julian calendar year, stored in a 16-bit signed field. Provides arithmetic with years duration, comparisons, range info, leap-year check (Julian rule: divisible by 4), and streaming.

Represents a day-of-week (0..6; Sun..Sat). Constructible from counts or from sys_days/local_days. Supports arithmetic with days, comparisons, and bracket operators to make weekday_indexed and weekday_last.
Pairs a weekday with an occurrence index within a month (1..5), e.g., the 3rd Monday. Used in month_weekday and year_month_weekday.
Represents the last occurrence of a given weekday within a month (e.g., last Friday).
A pair of year and month in the Julian calendar. Supports arithmetic with months/years, comparisons, streaming, and ok() validation.
Represents a month and day within a year (no year). Used to compose dates; ok() validates day against month (Feb allows 29).
Represents the last day of a given month (year-independent). Combined with a year to form a concrete date (year_month_day_last).
Represents an occurrence of a weekday within a month (e.g., third Tuesday of some month, without year).
Represents the last occurrence of a specified weekday within a given month (no year).
A full date in the Julian calendar with year, month, and day. Convertible to/from sys_days/local_days, supports arithmetic with months/years, comparisons, and validity checking.
Represents “the last day of a specific month in a specific year.” Provides conversion to sys_days/local_days and arithmetic with months/years.
Represents a specific occurrence of a weekday within a given month and year (e.g., second Monday of March 2024). Convertible to/from sys_days/local_days and supports arithmetic with months/years.
Represents the last occurrence of a weekday in a specified month and year (e.g., last Friday of Nov 2025). Convertible to sys_days/local_days and supports month/year arithmetic.
Tag type used to denote "the last" day or weekday within a month when composing Islamic calendar dates (e.g., month/last, year/month/last). Has no state.
Represents a day-of-month in the Islamic calendar. Valid range is 1..30 as per ok(). Lightweight value type with arithmetic by islamic::days. Stream insertion prints zero-padded two digits.
Represents a month of the Islamic calendar (1..12). Supports arithmetic with islamic::months, wraparound within year. Stream insertion prints localized month names.
Represents an Islamic year (stored in 16-bit signed). Provides arithmetic with islamic::years, range helpers, and leap-year test per Islamic tabular calendar. ok() always true.

Represents day of week (0..6). Constructible from unsigned or from sys_days/local_days. Provides arithmetic by islamic::days and composition to weekday_indexed or weekday_last. Stream insertion prints Arabic weekday names.
Pairs a weekday with an index 1..5 (e.g., 2nd Friday) for the Islamic calendar. Used to compose month/weekday_indexed and year/month/weekday[index].
Designates the last occurrence of a given weekday within a month (e.g., month/weekday[last]). Wraps a weekday.
Represents a year and month in the Islamic calendar. Provides arithmetic by months and years and comparison operations. Streams as YYYY/MonthName.
Represents a month/day (no year) in the Islamic calendar. ok() validates against month lengths of the tabular calendar (last month has 30 days).
Represents the last day of a given Islamic month (year-independent). Used in composing year/month/last and conversions.
Represents a rule like "nth weekday of a month" (e.g., 3rd Friday of Sha'ban).
Represents the last occurrence of a weekday within a month (e.g., last Friday of Ramadan).

Full Islamic calendar date (year, month, day). Constructible from components, from year_month_day_last, or from sys_days/local_days via conversion. Provides arithmetic, validation, and conversion to time points.

objects.description: Enum to disambiguate how to resolve ambiguous or nonexistent local times when converting between local and system time. earliest selects the earlier mapping; latest selects the later mapping.
A tag type used internally as an overload/disambiguation token. No data or behavior is defined here.
Holds time zone rule information over a half-open interval [begin, end) in system time: UTC offset, DST save, and abbreviation in effect.
Describes how a local time maps to system time: unique (single mapping), nonexistent (gap), or ambiguous (overlap). For gaps/overlaps, first and second provide the adjacent sys_info segments.
Exception thrown when attempting to convert a local time that falls in a spring-forward gap. Carries a formatted diagnostic message.
Exception thrown when a local time maps to two instants (fall-back overlap) and an explicit choice is required.

Represents a named IANA time zone. Provides conversions between local and system (UTC) time and access to rule info. Constructed internally from database records; public explicit constructor is tagged with detail::undocumented.
Represents a link/alias entry in the TZ database mapping one name to a target zone. Only present when not using the OS TZDB.
Represents a single leap second insertion event. Stores its effective system time and reports a fixed value() of 1 second.

Holds a snapshot of the time zone database: version string, list of zones, links (if not OS TZDB), leap seconds, optional rules and Windows mappings. Forms a singly-linked list via next to support hot-reload.

Specialization providing identity conversion for system_clock time_points.

Specialization converting system_clock time to utc_clock time via utc_clock::from_sys.
Specialization converting utc_clock time to system_clock time via utc_clock::to_sys.

Specialization converting utc_clock time to local_t time via utc_clock::to_local.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# We need to generate bytes that will be used both as a format string and as data string.
# The fuzz stubs parse/format using Howard Hinnant date.h directives. We'll generate pairs
# concatenated with a separator so the harness can pick either as FUZZ_PARAM_STR independently.
# Since we only return one buffer, it should contain a variety of candidate lines separated by newlines.
# The harness will sample strings from the buffer; typical fuzzers split by NUL or provide entire buffer.
# To be robust, we will include multiple NUL-terminated segments: alternating fmt and data examples.
# Each segment will be valid UTF-8/ASCII, with patterns covering dates, times, offsets, and zones.

TZ_ABBREVS = [
    b"UTC", b"GMT", b"PST", b"PDT", b"EST", b"EDT", b"CET", b"CEST",
    b"EET", b"MSK", b"IST", b"JST", b"AEST", b"ACDT", b"Z"
]

# Build diverse format directives supported by date.h
CORE_DIRECTIVES = [
    b"%Y", b"%m", b"%d", b"%H", b"%M", b"%S", b"%z", b"%Z",
    b"%F",  # %Y-%m-%d
    b"%T",  # %H:%M:%S
    b"%R",  # %H:%M
    b"%D",  # %m/%d/%y
]

DATEH_EXT = [
    b"%Ez",  # +hh:mm
    b"%E*z", # accepts both %z and %Ez
    b"%EX",  # locale date rep (date.h often maps to %m/%d/%y)
    b"%EX %T",
    b"%F %T",
    b"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z",
    b"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z",
    b"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%S",  # fractional printed width handled by date.h

def rand_int(rng: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(a, b)


def rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    return rng.choice(seq)


def build_format(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Randomly assemble a format string with 2-6 parts
    parts = []
    n = rand_int(rng, 2, 6)
    for _ in range(n):
        kind = rng.random()
        if kind < 0.55:
            parts.append(rand_choice(rng, CORE_DIRECTIVES))
        elif kind < 0.85:
            parts.append(rand_choice(rng, DATEH_EXT))
        else:
            parts.append(rand_choice(rng, LITERALS))

    if b"%" not in fmt:

        fmt = (fmt + b" %F").strip()

def pad2(n: int) -> bytes:
    return f"{n:02d}".encode()


def pad4(n: int) -> bytes:
    return f"{n:04d}".encode()


def build_offset(rng: random.Random, extended: bool) -> bytes:
    # Build numeric UTC offset: +HHMM or +HH:MM
    sign = b"+" if rng.random() < 0.5 else b"-"
    hh = rand_int(rng, 0, 23)
    mm = rand_int(rng, 0, 59)
    if extended:
        return sign + pad2(hh) + b":" + pad2(mm)
    else:
        return sign + pad2(hh) + pad2(mm)


def build_datetime(rng: random.Random, need_time: bool) -> bytes:
    # Construct a plausible date/time
    year = rand_int(rng, 1600, 2400)
    month = rand_int(rng, 1, 12)
    # choose day valid for month roughly
    dim = [31, 29 if month == 2 else 30][1] if month in (4,6,9,11,2) else 31
    if month == 2:
        dim = 29 if (year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0)) else 28
    day = rand_int(rng, 1, dim)
    date = pad4(year) + b"-" + pad2(month) + b"-" + pad2(day)
    if not need_time and rng.random() < 0.5:
        return date
    h = rand_int(rng, 0, 23)
    m = rand_int(rng, 0, 59)
    s = rand_int(rng, 0, 59)
    # sometimes fractional seconds
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        frac_width = rand_int(rng, 1, 6)
        frac = ("%0"+str(frac_width)+"d") % rand_int(rng, 0, 10**frac_width - 1)
        frac_b = b"." + frac.encode()
    else:
        frac_b = b""
    time = pad2(h) + b":" + pad2(m) + b":" + pad2(s) + frac_b
    sep = b"T" if rng.random() < 0.5 else b" "
    dt = date + sep + time
    # optionally append space and TZ or offset
    r = rng.random()
    if r < 0.33:
        dt += b" " + rand_choice(rng, TZ_ABBREVS)
    elif r < 0.66:
        dt += b" " + build_offset(rng, extended=True)
    else:
        dt += b" " + build_offset(rng, extended=False)
    return dt


def build_data_for_format(rng: random.Random, fmt: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Heuristic builder: cover common directives present in fmt
    s = b""
    contains = lambda token: token in fmt
    # Date baseline
    year = rand_int(rng, 1970, 2100)
    month = rand_int(rng, 1, 12)
    dim = 31
    if month in (4, 6, 9, 11):
        dim = 30
    elif month == 2:
        dim = 29 if (year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0)) else 28
    day = rand_int(rng, 1, dim)
    hour = rand_int(rng, 0, 23)
    minute = rand_int(rng, 0, 59)
    second = rand_int(rng, 0, 59)

    # Compose according to presence of compound tokens first
    if contains(b"%F %T") or (contains(b"%F") and contains(b"%T")):
        s = pad4(year)+b"-"+pad2(month)+b"-"+pad2(day)+b" "+pad2(hour)+b":"+pad2(minute)+b":"+pad2(second)
    elif contains(b"%F"):
        s = pad4(year)+b"-"+pad2(month)+b"-"+pad2(day)
    elif contains(b"%T"):
        s = pad2(hour)+b":"+pad2(minute)+b":"+pad2(second)
    elif contains(b"%R"):
        s = pad2(hour)+b":"+pad2(minute)
    elif contains(b"%D"):
        s = pad2(month)+b"/"+pad2(day)+b"/"+f"{year%100:02d}".encode()
    else:
        # Fallback comprehensive ISO-like
        s = build_datetime(rng, need_time=True)

    # Offsets and zones
    if contains(b"%Ez"):
        s += b" " + build_offset(rng, extended=True)
    elif contains(b"%E*z"):
        s += b" " + (build_offset(rng, extended=True) if rng.random()<0.5 else build_offset(rng, extended=False))
    elif contains(b"%z") and b"%Ez" not in fmt:
        s += b" " + build_offset(rng, extended=False)
    if contains(b"%Z"):
        s += b" " + rand_choice(rng, TZ_ABBREVS)

    # If nothing time-related, sometimes append time to give parser more fields
    if not any(contains(t) for t in (b"%H", b"%M", b"%S", b"%T", b"%R")) and rng.random() < 0.3:
        s += b" " + pad2(hour)+b":"+pad2(minute)

    return s


def assemble_segments(rng: random.Random, count: int) -> bytes:
    # Build multiple NUL-terminated segments, alternating fmt and data variants.
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(count):
        fmt = build_format(rng)
        data = build_data_for_format(rng, fmt)
        # Ensure C-string termination for each so fuzzer can extract cleanly
        chunks.append(fmt + b"\x00")
        chunks.append(data + b"\x00")
    # Also include some canonical pairs to broaden coverage
    canonical = [
        (b"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z", build_datetime(rng, True)),
        (b"%F", build_datetime(rng, False).split(b" ")[0]),
        (b"%T", b"12:34:56"),
        (b"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z", b"2020-06-30 23:59:60 UTC"),  # leap second textual
    ]
    for f, d in canonical:
        chunks.append(f + b"\x00")
        chunks.append(d + b"\x00")

    blob = b"".join(chunks)
    # Limit size
    return blob[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Number of segments varies with seed for diversity
    count = 4 + (seed % 5)
    return assemble_segments(rng, count)

def _with_literal_abbrev(fmt: str, abbrev: str) -> str:

    choices = [

def _build_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pool: List[str] = []
    pool.extend(_BASE_FORMATS)

    # Enrich pool with literals
    for _ in range(20):

        "[%a %b %e %T %Y] %Z",
    ])

    # Ensure uniqueness but keep order somewhat random
    rng.shuffle(pool)
    # Trim to a reasonable sample size
    return pool[:64]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:

    pool = _build_pool(rng)
    fmt = rng.choice(pool)
    # Ensure length <= 4096 bytes
    data = fmt.encode('utf-8')[:4096]
    return data

# Target datatype: numeric timezone offset seconds (whole seconds, typically within ±86400)
# Fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() as a format string for date::to_stream(..., "%z", zoned_time)
# Our strategy: generate a plausible C-style format string that exercises a wide
# range of date formatting directives, especially those that request numeric
# timezone offsets (%z, %Ez, %Oz, %Z), while remaining valid. We also include
# width/flags and literals. The generator returns bytes containing a single
# NUL-terminated format string for FUZZ_PARAM_STR().
#
# We avoid invalid specifiers to reduce exceptions; we mix directives from
# Howard Hinnant date format extensions likely handled by date::to_stream.

_DIRECTIVES_CORE = [
    "%Y", "%y", "%C", "%m", "%d", "%e", "%j",
    "%H", "%I", "%M", "%S", "%f", "%R", "%T", "%D",
    "%u", "%w", "%V", "%G", "%g",

_DIRECTIVES_TZ = [
    "%z",  # +hhmm numeric offset
    "%Ez", # +hh:mm extended
    "%Oz", # +hh:mm (alternative, some impls treat same as %Ez)
    "%Z",  # abbreviation
]

# Weekday/month names etc. (safe literals and named fields)
_DIRECTIVES_TEXT = ["%a", "%A", "%b", "%h", "%B", "%p"]

# Literal helpers
_LITERALS = [
    " ", "-", "/", ":", ".", ", ", "T", "Z", "[", "]", "(", ")",
]

# Width and flags applicable to some numeric fields; we only combine with
# directives that are commonly width-tolerant (numbers). We omit invalid combos.
_WIDTHS = ["", "%1", "%2", "%3", "%4", "%5"]  # placeholders; handled differently

# Some composite templates known to work across date::to_stream
_TEMPLATES = [
    "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S%Ez",                 # ISO 8601 extended with offset
    "%FT%T%Ez",                             # RFC3339-like
    "%a, %d %b %Y %T %Z",                  # RFC1123-like
    "%Y-%m-%d %T %z",                      # Basic offset

    "%Y-%j %H:%M:%S.%f%Ez",                # Ordinal day + subseconds
    "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M%Ez",                   # No seconds
    "%Y-%m-%d %R %Z",                      # %R = %H:%M
]

# Build a random but sane format by mixing directives and literals.

def _rand_pick(rng, seq):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _build_random_format(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide between using a known-good template or composing a custom one
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        fmt = _rand_pick(rng, _TEMPLATES)
    else:
        parts = []
        # Ensure we include at least one timezone directive for the target
        tz_inserted = False
        count = rng.randint(3, 10)
        for i in range(count):
            choice_pool = []
            # Bias to include timezone once
            if not tz_inserted and (i == count - 1 or rng.random() < 0.35):
                parts.append(_rand_pick(rng, _DIRECTIVES_TZ))
                tz_inserted = True
                continue
            # Otherwise pick among core/text/literals
            r = rng.random()
            if r < 0.55:
                parts.append(_rand_pick(rng, _DIRECTIVES_CORE))
            elif r < 0.8:
                parts.append(_rand_pick(rng, _DIRECTIVES_TEXT))
            else:
                # Add 1-2 literals
                lit_count = 1 if rng.random() < 0.7 else 2
                lits = ''.join(_rand_pick(rng, _LITERALS) for _ in range(lit_count))
                parts.append(lits)
        if not tz_inserted:
            parts.append(_rand_pick(rng, _DIRECTIVES_TZ))
        # Sprinkle separators
        sep = _rand_pick(rng, [" ", "T", " "])
        fmt = sep.join(parts)

    # Optionally wrap with brackets or add trailing newline-free suffix
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        fmt = "[" + fmt + "]"
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        fmt = fmt + " (UTC%z)"
    return fmt


def _maybe_pad(rng: random.Random, fmt: str) -> str:
    # Sometimes prepend or append harmless literals to exercise parser
    prefixes = ["", "", "", "%Y-", "date:", "@", "on "]
    suffixes = ["", "", "", "", " %Z", "", ""]
    return _rand_pick(rng, prefixes) + fmt + _rand_pick(rng, suffixes)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create multiple candidate formats and pick one to vary outputs per seed
    candidates = []
    k = rng.randint(3, 7)
    for _ in range(k):
        f = _build_random_format(rng)
        f = _maybe_pad(rng, f)
        candidates.append(f)

    fmt = _rand_pick(rng, candidates)

    # Ensure it's not empty and within size limit, and NUL-terminated for C APIs
    s = fmt[:4090]  # leave room for NUL
    if not s:
        s = "%Y-%m-%d %T%Ez"
    return (s + "\x00").encode("utf-8")

    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Optionally generate multiple candidates separated by newlines to give the fuzzer more options in one buffer.
    # However, stubs read a single FUZZ_PARAM_STR per call, which consumes the whole buffer; keep it to one.
    candidate = _build_candidate(r)
    # Return as UTF-8 bytes without trailing NUL; add a newline to mimic typical line-oriented inputs rarely
    if _random_bool(r, 0.2) and not candidate.endswith("\n"):
        candidate += "\n"
    return candidate.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

# This generator produces a bytes blob that contains two C-strings concatenated:
# fmt\0data
# The fuzzer stub calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR twice; many harnesses split the provided
# initial buffer on a NUL to feed successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. By packing
# fmt and data separated by a NUL and ending with a final NUL, we maximize the
# chance both receive coherent values.
#
# We focus on Howard Hinnant date::from_stream format specifiers, which largely
# mirror C/POSIX strftime, plus extended items used by the library:
#  %Y (year), %m (month), %d (day), %H (hour), %M (minute), %S (second),
#  %T (HH:MM:SS), %F (YYYY-MM-DD), %z (numeric offset), %Z (abbr),
#  %a/%A (weekday names), %b/%B (month names), %j (yearday),
#  %u/%w (weekday number), literal text, spaces, and brackets used by the lib
#  for optional components. We generate multiple coherent combinations.
#
# We include several families of formats to exercise:
#  - Date only (Y-m-d and variants)
#  - Date + time (T, or H:M:S)
#  - Time only
#  - With timezone offset %z and/or abbreviation %Z
#  - Week-based components and month names
#  - Fractional seconds using %S and a custom ".ffffff" literal
#  - Bracketed optional fields used by the library parsing (it treats literal
#    text transparently)
#
# For utc_time we also allow %Z/%z to populate abbrev/offset.

MONTH_ABBR = ["Jan","Feb","Mar","Apr","May","Jun","Jul","Aug","Sep","Oct","Nov","Dec"]
MONTH_FULL = [
    "January","February","March","April","May","June",
    "July","August","September","October","November","December"
]
WEEKDAY_ABBR = ["Sun","Mon","Tue","Wed","Thu","Fri","Sat"]
WEEKDAY_FULL = ["Sunday","Monday","Tuesday","Wednesday","Thursday","Friday","Saturday"]
TZ_ABBR = [
    "UTC","GMT","PST","PDT","MST","MDT","CST","CDT","EST","EDT",
    "CET","CEST","EET","EEST","IST","JST","AEST","AEDT","NZST","NZDT"
]

def _rand_dt(rng: random.Random) -> datetime:
    # Choose a broad year range within 0001..9999 supported by datetime
    year = rng.randint(1600, 9999)
    # Random day in year
    start = datetime(year, 1, 1, tzinfo=None)
    # Max 365/366
    days_in_year = 366 if (year % 4 == 0 and (year % 100 != 0 or year % 400 == 0)) else 365
    d = rng.randrange(days_in_year)
    dt = start + timedelta(days=d,
                           hours=rng.randrange(24),
                           minutes=rng.randrange(60),
                           seconds=rng.randrange(60))
    return dt

def _rand_offset(rng: random.Random):
    # Generate plausible UTC offset in minutes, typical zone ranges
    # Quarter-hour increments common in some zones
    hours = rng.randint(-12, 14)
    # common minute offsets: 0, 15, 30, 45
    mins = rng.choice([0, 15, 30, 45])
    # Normalize sign
    sign = 1 if hours >= 0 else -1
    total = hours * 60 + sign * mins
    # Bound to plausible range [-12:00, +14:00]
    total = max(-12*60, min(14*60, total))
    return total

def _fmt_offset_z(total_minutes: int) -> str:
    # %z expects +HHMM or -HHMM
    sign = '+' if total_minutes >= 0 else '-'
    mm = abs(total_minutes)
    h = mm // 60
    m = mm % 60
    return f"{sign}{h:02d}{m:02d}"

def _choose_format_and_data(rng: random.Random):
    dt = _rand_dt(rng)
    # maybe attach an offset and/or abbreviation
    use_z = rng.random() < 0.7
    use_Z = rng.random() < 0.5
    off_min = _rand_offset(rng) if use_z else 0
    tzabbr = rng.choice(TZ_ABBR) if use_Z else None

    families = []

    # 1) ISO date only
    families.append(("%F", dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")))

    # 2) ISO date + time T
    families.append(("%FT%T", dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")))

    # 3) RFC-like with space and seconds
    families.append(("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")))

    # 4) Month name, day, year
    fmt4 = "%B %d, %Y"
    data4 = f"{MONTH_FULL[dt.month-1]} {dt.day:02d}, {dt.year:04d}"
    families.append((fmt4, data4))

    # 5) Weekday name, abbreviated month, day and time
    fmt5 = "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S"
    data5 = f"{WEEKDAY_ABBR[dt.weekday()]} , {dt.day:02d} {MONTH_ABBR[dt.month-1]} {dt.year:04d} {dt.hour:02d}:{dt.minute:02d}:{dt.second:02d}"
    # Intentionally include a space before comma to exercise literal tolerance
    families.append((fmt5, data5))

    # 6) Time only
    families.append(("%T", dt.strftime("%H:%M:%S")))

    # 7) Ordinal day of year
    doy = (dt - datetime(dt.year,1,1)).days + 1
    fmt7 = "%Y-%j %H:%M:%S"
    data7 = f"{dt.year:04d}-{doy:03d} {dt.hour:02d}:{dt.minute:02d}:{dt.second:02d}"
    families.append((fmt7, data7))

    # 8) With offset %z
    if use_z:
        base_fmt = rng.choice(["%FT%T", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", "%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y"])  # variety
        base_data = {
            "%FT%T": dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
            "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S": dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
            "%a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y": f"{WEEKDAY_ABBR[dt.weekday()]} {MONTH_ABBR[dt.month-1]} {dt.day:02d} {dt.hour:02d}:{dt.minute:02d}:{dt.second:02d} {dt.year:04d}",
        }[base_fmt]
        fmt8 = base_fmt + " %z"
        data8 = f"{base_data} {_fmt_offset_z(off_min)}"
        families.append((fmt8, data8))

    # 9) With abbreviation %Z (may be ignored or mapped by tz DB)
    if use_Z:
        base_fmt = rng.choice(["%FT%T", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"])  # simpler
        base_data = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S") if base_fmt == "%FT%T" else dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
        fmt9 = base_fmt + " %Z"
        data9 = f"{base_data} {tzabbr}"
        families.append((fmt9, data9))

    # 10) Both %z and %Z
    if use_z and use_Z:
        base_fmt = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"
        base_data = dt.strftime(base_fmt)
        fmt10 = base_fmt + " %z %Z"
        data10 = f"{base_data} {_fmt_offset_z(off_min)} {tzabbr}"
        families.append((fmt10, data10))

    # 11) Fractional seconds via literal .ffffff (parser accepts literals)
    # date::from_stream supports %S with subseconds if format includes %[...f]
    # but as a general approach, provide a literal fractional part; many parsers
    # accept it. Keep width between 3..9
    frac_width = rng.randint(3, 9)
    frac = ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(frac_width))
    fmt11 = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S" + "." + "x"*frac_width  # use literal placeholders
    data11 = dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S") + "." + frac
    families.append((fmt11, data11))

    # 12) Bracketed literal text to exercise literal matching
    fmt12 = "[on ]%A, %B %d %Y at %H:%M:%S"
    data12 = f"on {WEEKDAY_FULL[dt.weekday()]}, {MONTH_FULL[dt.month-1]} {dt.day:02d} {dt.year:04d} at {dt.hour:02d}:{dt.minute:02d}:{dt.second:02d}"
    families.append((fmt12, data12))

    # Choose one family
    fmt, data = rng.choice(families)

    # Occasionally shuffle whitespace or add trailing spaces to test robustness
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        data = data + (" " * rng.randint(1, 3))
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        fmt = fmt + (" " * rng.randint(1, 2))

    return fmt, data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    fmt, data = _choose_format_and_data(rng)

    # Compose as two C-strings: fmt\0data\0
    blob = (fmt + "\0" + data + "\0").encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    # Ensure size limit
    return blob[:4096]
